summary: Premium farmer-friendly React frontend for tomato crop analysis, integrated with the existing FastAPI prediction API. The existing backend directory is preserved unchanged.

questions.question: Which language should the TomatoGuard AI frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed React development with stronger component and API contracts.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: React development with standard JavaScript syntax.

questions.rationale: A modular dashboard with a multipart API integration benefits from typed data models and safer refactoring.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and tooling should be used?

options.label: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS
options.description: Fast client-side React app with utility-first responsive styling.

options.label: React + Vite + CSS Modules
options.description: React with locally scoped styles and no Tailwind dependency.

questions.rationale: This is the requested frontend stack.

questions.question: Which frontend capabilities should be included?
questions.recommendedChoice: Dashboard, Analyze Crop, AI Results, Insights, Recommendations, History, How AI Works; Lucide React; Framer Motion; React Router; multipart POST to http://127.0.0.1:8001/predict using file; localStorage history; modular reusable components; responsive farmer-friendly UI; no fake prediction data
questions.answer: Dashboard, Analyze Crop, AI Results, Insights, Recommendations, History, How AI Works; Lucide React; Framer Motion; React Router; multipart POST to http://127.0.0.1:8001/predict using file; localStorage history; modular reusable components; responsive farmer-friendly UI; no fake prediction data
questions.rationale: These are the explicit requested product and integration requirements.

sharedQuestions.question: Which persistent data stores are required?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use browser localStorage for client-side history; no provisioned datastore.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Managed relational persistence for shared application data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for uploaded images or media.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The requested frontend stores history locally and sends images to the existing API; no new shared persistence is requested.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before using application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: Allow the local farmer workflow without sign-in.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The request specifies a local frontend and existing unauthenticated FastAPI endpoint without an authentication requirement.

backendConstraint: Preserve c:\tomato_sih\backend unchanged. The frontend consumes the existing POST /predict endpoint only.
